title: The fish sign
hookLine: a fish, two curved lines: in Greek, its letters spell the initials of Jesus Christ, God's Son, Savior
last: AWAKE, CREATIVE, GLAD TO BE IN A BODY.

cards: Two curved lines, crossing at one end. A child can draw it in the sand. It turns up on the backs of cars, on necklaces, on bakery signs and business cards, telling you, roughly, that somebody here is a Christian.
But why a fish? It isn't a cross, a lamb or a dove. It's lunch.
And the answer is a word puzzle, hidden in plain sight, in Greek.

teach.b: The Greek word for fish is ichthys. Five letters: iota, chi, theta, upsilon, sigma. Take each as the first letter of a word, and you get a creed.
Iesous: Jesus. Christos: Christ. Theou: of God.
Huios: Son. Soter: Savior. Jesus Christ, God's Son, Savior.
Augustine, in the City of God, spells out the five Greek words, says their first letters make ichthys, fish, and that Christ is understood in the word.

Then he adds a picture: Christ could live without sin in the deep waters of this mortal life, the way a fish lives in the depths. Earlier still, a North African writer named Tertullian makes the fish a picture of baptism.

In his book on baptism he calls Christians little fishes, born in water, following our Ichthys, Jesus Christ. And fish swim through the Gospels too. Jesus calls fishermen: "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."

teach.h: FISHERS OF MEN, LOAVES AND FISHES.
teach.b: He feeds crowds with loaves and fishes. After the resurrection, in John's Gospel, he cooks fish on a beach for his friends. Now, the secret part.
Tradition says early Christians scratched the fish on walls and tombs.
And there's a story told today: in times of danger, one stranger would draw one curve in the dust, and if the other drew the second, they knew they were safe together.
It's a good story, but the ancient writers quoted here don't tell it. What they show is a sign explained openly, in books anyone could read.

teach.h: A SECRET, LIKE A FAMILY JOKE.
teach.b: A secret, maybe, the way a family's private joke is: you have to be inside to get it.

how: Some Christians use the fish symbol on jewelry, cars, signs and church art as a quiet sign of faith, and some teach children the five Greek words behind it.

games.q: a friend sees a fish on a necklace and asks why a fish stands for Jesus. what do you tell them?
o: it was only a password, nothing more.
its Greek letters begin five words: Jesus Christ, God's Son, Savior.
games.why: ichthys: five letters, five words. Augustine spells it out, and Tertullian adds the little fishes born in the water of baptism.

practice: With a finger on the table, a pen on paper, or in the air, draw one curve, then the other, crossing at the tail, and trace it slowly, again and again. Let the five words go by with it if you like: Jesus, Christ, God's, Son, Savior.
If you pray, those five words can be your prayer, nothing added; if not, keep tracing, and notice how small a thing can carry a whole meaning.
